dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Did you see those trẻ trâu in the park yesterday? They were screaming so loudly I couldn't read my book.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: The trẻ trâu in Vietnam are different from those in Russia. In my homeland, children are rarely allowed to be noisy in public places. But I find them dễ thương, they seem to be having fun.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Dễ thương? Those trẻ trâu made me spill my coffee! I really don't understand why Vietnamese parents let their children run around uncontrolled like that.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Not all Vietnamese children are trẻ trâu. You shouldn't judge other people's văn hóa based on a few cases. Maybe you don't fully understand life here yet.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Perhaps you're right. I notice you seem to care a lot about children. Do you like kids?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: I... I just think each văn hóa has its own way of raising children. Why are you asking if I like children?
